blindSummary:
This country's religious penal code contains one of the world's most explicit trans-specific criminal provisions: one section creates an offence of "a man posing as a woman or vice versa", and the government has confirmed in its official guidance that the code applies to all persons in the country including tourists — travel agents are briefed accordingly. A separate indecency provision criminalises clothing that "tarnishes the image of the state religion" with fines and imprisonment, and same-sex intimacy carries a stoning sentence (under a formal moratorium since 2019, with whipping and long prison terms actively available).

Enforcement is quiet rather than predatory — no prosecution of a foreign visitor under these provisions has been documented — but the country is an absolute monarchy with heavy surveillance, censorship, and no LGBT organising of any kind, and LGBT people from the country have fled abroad. The legal exposure for a discovered trans visitor is categorical: no recognition, no protection, and gender expression itself is a written offence.
blindOutOfScope: No current travel advisory flags general security risks; the hazards here are legal, not criminal.
